faqs.a: Answer: The high-quality PU panels distributed by ADIS use molds taken from real rock, with reliefs that replicate cracks, veins, natural weathering and even mineral inclusions. From 1-2 meters away, they're virtually indistinguishable from natural stone. The key is in the installation: a good installer varies the placement pattern, alternates orientations and uses decorative filler in the joints to simulate a real stone installation. In interiors with ambient lighting, the effect is striking. The difference shows up to the touch (lighter and slightly warmer) and when tapped (sounds hollow vs. solid). For applications where direct contact is minimal (accent walls, entry façades), PU panels deliver 95% of the visual impact at 20% of the cost and weight.

faqs.q: Do I need to reinforce my wall to install PU panels or flexible stone veneer?
faqs.a: Answer: Generally NO. PU panels weigh approximately 2.5 kg/m² and flexible stone veneer about 4 kg/m². To put it in perspective: a coat of high-quality latex paint weighs ~1.5 kg/m² per layer. These coverings weigh less than two coats of paint. Any wall that can hold paint can hold these coverings with no problem. The only consideration is that the surface must be solid: don't install over damaged drywall, walls with structural moisture or surfaces with peeling paint. If your wall is in good condition, you can install directly over the existing finish (plaster, concrete, block, brick) with the appropriate adhesive.

faqs.q: How long does it take to install a wall of stone-look PU panels?
faqs.a: Answer: A professional installer can lay 20-30 m² of PU panels in an 8-hour workday. For a typical living room accent wall (e.g. 4 m wide × 2.5 m high = 10 m²), installation takes half a day including preparation. Compared to natural stone, which requires: support structure (+1 day), mesh placement (+0.5 days), stone installation (+2-3 days), and jointing (+1 day) — PU panels represent an 80-90% savings in construction time. Plus, they generate no stone-cutting dust and require no heavy specialized tools.

faqs.q: Does WPC Wall Cladding really require no maintenance in the Sonora climate?
faqs.a: Answer: Correct. WPC Wall Cladding is designed to withstand the most extreme climates with no maintenance. Specifically: (1) Intense sun: The WPC compound includes UV stabilizers that prevent fading. (2) Monsoon rains: It's 100% waterproof — doesn't absorb water, doesn't swell, doesn't rot. (3) Temperature swings: It handles expansion and contraction without cracking (unlike wood). The only recommended "maintenance" is a wash with soap and water every 6-12 months to remove accumulated dust. You never need to varnish, seal, sand or repaint — ever. In accelerated aging tests, WPC cladding maintains its aesthetic and structural properties after simulating 25 years of outdoor exposure.

faqs.q: Can I combine different types of cladding on the same façade?
faqs.a: Answer: Absolutely! In fact, it's one of the most striking design trends. Some combinations we've executed in Nogales and Tucson projects with excellent results: (1) Teak WPC Cladding on the lower part of the façade + stone-look PU panels on the upper part = a modern, warm look. (2) Volcanic flagstone PU panels on the entry wall + Stone Gray WPC Cladding on the sides = spectacular textural contrast. (3) Flexible stone veneer on the main façade + PU panels on interior accent walls = exterior-interior coherence. At ADIS we offer free design consulting to help you combine textures and colors. We can create 3D renders of your façade with the different options before you make a decision.

curiosos.title: From real wood to "eternal wood"
curiosos.content: Decorative PVC, WPC and PU beams emerged as an answer to an age-old problem: natural wood beams are beautiful but demand constant tribute. Termites, moisture, warping, rot, peeling paint — every year, millions of dollars are spent maintaining wood beams that, sooner or later, succumb. In the 2000s, polymer composite technology matured enough to replicate not only the appearance but the tactile texture of real wood. Today, a WPC or PU beam can fool even an experienced carpenter... until they're told it's been installed for 10 years without a single drop of varnish.

curiosos.title: The 2.81 kg beam that carries the weight of tradition
curiosos.content: The 2,900 x 152 x 75 mm PU beam weighs only 2.81 kilograms. To put it in perspective: a real wood beam of the same dimensions would weigh approximately 12-15 kg. That means you can lift a PU beam with a single finger, while the wood one requires two people. This 80% weight reduction revolutionized ceiling décor, making it possible to install decorative beams on structures that could never support the weight of natural wood.

faqs.q: Are the beams structural? Can they hold up my roof?
faqs.a: No. WPC, PU and PVC beams are strictly decorative. They are not designed to bear structural loads, roof weight, or to be used as load-bearing construction elements. They are fastened to the existing ceiling (slab, drywall, drop ceiling) with screws or adhesive, but their function is purely aesthetic. If you need structural beams, you must consult a civil engineer.

faqs.q: What's the difference between WPC, PU and PVC?
faqs.a: | Material | What it is | Best for | |-|--|| | WPC | Wood Plastic Composite. Polymer blended with wood fiber. | Most realistic profile, longest warranty (15 years) | | PU | Polyurethane. Ultra-low-weight foamed material. | Fragile ceilings where weight is critical | | PVC | Polyvinyl chloride. Rigid polymer. | Best price, good durability, fire resistant |  In short: WPC = maximum realism and warranty. PU = minimum weight. PVC = best value for money.

faqs.q: Can I install them myself or do I need a professional?
faqs.a: WPC and PVC Profile beams can be installed by someone with basic DIY experience, though two people are recommended for safety when working at heights. PU beams are so light that one person can easily handle them alone. The most important things are: 1. Locate the ceiling joists to anchor correctly 2. Use a laser level for perfect alignment 3. Use a safe ladder or scaffold  If you don't feel comfortable working on ceilings, ADIS can recommend certified installers in Nogales and Tucson.

faqs.q: Do they look like real wood or can you tell they're plastic?
faqs.a: WPC beams have the most convincing realism thanks to the real wood fiber composite in their composition. At a normal viewing distance (1.5-3 meters), most people can't tell the difference. PU beams have a slightly more "uniform" finish that can give away their synthetic nature at very close range, but the overall effect is high quality. The key is in the installation: a well-installed, aligned beam with a decorative cap looks professional and elegant.

faqs.q: How many beams do I need for my ceiling?
faqs.a: It depends on the desired effect:  - Subtle effect: 3-4 cross beams in a 4x5 meter living room. - Full cabin effect: Beams every 60-80 cm, covering the whole ceiling. - Focal accent: 1-3 beams over a specific area (dining room, TV, bar).  Rule of thumb: Cross beams every 80-100 cm create a pleasant rhythm without overwhelming. For an exact calculation, come to ADIS with your space dimensions and we'll do a design at no cost.
